decisions.reason: The insufficient-ETH revert rule applies only to the ETH payment path and does not change direct USDC wallet minting.
The source preserves the existing $30 target and changes only handling of insufficient ETH, not the mint price or revenue allocation.
The existing feedback rule already requires a confirmed NFT mint before success feedback; specifying an insufficient-ETH revert does not change that rule.
ETH remains a supported wallet payment asset; the new insufficient-funds behavior is independently represented by the ETH pricing and refund Requirement.
The source does not change which payment methods are enabled, displayed, or selectable at checkout.
The Transak fiat flow converts fiat to USDC and is unaffected by the insufficient-ETH behavior of the wallet payment path.
The insufficient-ETH rule does not alter the NFT ebook format or its unlimited supply.
The source does not change the optional gratuity feature, its placement, or its available amounts.
The source decision does not explicitly require any FAQ copy change concerning insufficient ETH.
The insufficient-ETH revert rule does not change any current NFT metadata attribute or visibility requirement.
A reverted insufficient-ETH attempt is not a completed mint and the source does not change no-referral commission allocation.
The existing rule already limits reporting to finalized successful mints; an insufficient-ETH revert remains unsuccessful and requires no state change.
